_source_for_mould_advice: USDA guidance: firm produce (carrots, peppers, cabbage): cut off at least 1 inch around and below the mould spot; soft produce (cucumbers, peaches, tomatoes): discard. When in doubt, throw it out.

apple.fact: There are over 7,500 apple varieties grown around the world.
apple.store: Fridge crisper drawer, away from other produce: apples give off a gas that ripens things nearby.
apple.keeps: About 1–2 weeks on the counter, a month or more in the fridge.
apple.spoil: Soft or mushy spots, wrinkled skin, brown flesh, a fermented smell.

apricot.fact: A close relative of peaches and plums; Turkey grows more than any other country.
apricot.store: Ripen on the counter, then refrigerate.
apricot.keeps: A few days once ripe, about a week in the fridge.
apricot.spoil: Very soft, leaking juice, wrinkled or mouldy skin.

avocado.fact: Botanically a large berry with a single seed.
avocado.store: Ripen on the counter; refrigerate once ripe. Cut: keep the pit in and cover tightly.
avocado.keeps: Ripe: about 2–4 days in the fridge.
avocado.spoil: Mushy or hollow feel, dark stringy flesh, sour smell, mould at the stem.

banana.fact: Botanically a berry, and one of the most eaten fruits in the world.
banana.store: Room temperature, away from other fruit. Ripe ones can go in the fridge: the skin darkens but the inside keeps.
banana.keeps: Several days on the counter, a few more in the fridge once ripe.
banana.spoil: Mushy, leaking, fermented smell, mould at the stem. Brown spots alone just mean it's very ripe.

beetroot.fact: Its deep red colour comes from pigments called betalains.
beetroot.store: Cut off the leaves (leave a little stem) and refrigerate unwashed in a bag.
beetroot.spoil: Soft, wrinkled or slimy skin, mould.

bell pepper.fact: Red, yellow and orange peppers are usually green ones left to ripen longer.
bell pepper.store: Fridge crisper drawer, whole and unwashed.
bell pepper.spoil: Soft or wrinkled skin, sunken wet spots, mould.

blackberry.fact: Each berry is a cluster of tiny fruits called drupelets.
blackberry.store: Fridge, unwashed, in a single layer if you can. Wash just before eating.
blackberry.spoil: Mushy, leaking juice, grey fuzzy mould.

blueberry.fact: One of the few fruits native to North America.
blueberry.store: Fridge, unwashed, in a container that lets air in.
blueberry.spoil: Soft, shrivelled, leaking, white or grey mould.

broccoli.fact: The part we eat is a cluster of unopened flower buds.
broccoli.store: Fridge, unwashed, in a loose or open bag.
broccoli.spoil: Yellowing florets, slimy or limp stems, black spots, sour smell.

cabbage.fact: Sauerkraut and kimchi both start with cabbage.
cabbage.store: Fridge, whole and unwashed; wrap cut halves tightly.
cabbage.keeps: Whole: 1–2 weeks or more; cut: a few days.
cabbage.spoil: Slimy or black leaves, soft spots, strong sour smell. Peel off limp outer leaves; the inside is often fine.

cantaloupe.fact: Its netted skin is why it's also called a muskmelon.
cantaloupe.store: Ripen whole on the counter, then refrigerate. Scrub the rind before cutting; refrigerate cut melon right away.
cantaloupe.keeps: Ripe whole: about 5 days in the fridge; cut: about 3 days.
cantaloupe.spoil: Very soft or wet spots, sour or fermented smell, mould, a sunken stem end.

carrot.fact: Early carrots were purple or yellow; orange ones became popular in the 1600s Netherlands.
carrot.store: Cut off the green tops and refrigerate in a bag.
carrot.spoil: Slimy, mushy, very bendy or mouldy. A white blush on the surface is just drying.

cauliflower.fact: Like broccoli, it's a head of unopened flower buds.
cauliflower.store: Fridge, unwashed, stem side down in a loose bag.
cauliflower.spoil: Spreading brown or black spots, soft or slimy patches, an off smell.

celery.fact: Mostly water, with plenty of crunch for very few calories.
celery.store: Fridge, wrapped in foil or in a bag.
celery.spoil: Limp, hollow, slimy or very brown stalks.

cherry.fact: Sweet and sour cherries are different species.
cherry.spoil: Soft, wrinkled, leaking or mouldy fruit.

chili pepper.fact: The heat comes from capsaicin, packed into the pale ribs inside.
chili pepper.store: Fridge, dry, in a paper bag or container.
chili pepper.spoil: Soft, wrinkled, slimy or mouldy skin.

coconut.fact: Botanically a drupe, not a nut.
coconut.store: Whole: room temperature. Opened or grated: fridge, covered.
coconut.keeps: Whole: several weeks; opened: about 3–5 days.
coconut.spoil: Leaking, mould around the eyes, sour or soapy smell, slimy or yellow flesh.

corn.fact: Each strand of silk connects to a single kernel.
corn.store: Fridge, in the husk. Eat it soon: it loses sweetness fast.
corn.spoil: Slimy or mouldy kernels, sour smell, dried brown husk.

cucumber.store: Fridge, dry, wrapped to keep moisture in.
cucumber.spoil: Soft, wrinkled, slimy or mouldy skin, sunken wet spots.

date.fact: Date palms have been grown for thousands of years in the Middle East and North Africa.
date.store: Airtight container; the fridge keeps them even longer.
date.spoil: Sour or fermented smell or fuzzy mould. White sugar spots on the skin are normal.

dragon fruit.fact: The fruit of a cactus, also called pitaya.
dragon fruit.store: Ripen on the counter; refrigerate once ripe or cut.
dragon fruit.keeps: Ripe: about 3–5 days in the fridge.
dragon fruit.spoil: Mushy or brown flesh, shrivelled skin, sour smell, mould.

eggplant.fact: Botanically a berry, related to tomatoes and potatoes.
eggplant.store: A cool spot or the fridge crisper for a few days; it doesn't like the cold for long.
eggplant.spoil: Soft or wrinkled skin, mushy brown flesh, mould at the cap.

fig.fact: A fig is really a cluster of tiny flowers turned inward.
fig.spoil: Sour smell, oozing, mould, very mushy.

garlic.fact: A bulb usually holds 10 to 20 cloves.
garlic.store: Cool, dry, dark, airy place, not the fridge.
garlic.keeps: Whole bulbs: a few months; loose cloves: about 1–3 weeks.
garlic.spoil: Soft, shrivelled or brown cloves, mould. Green sprouts are safe but taste bitter.

ginger.fact: A rhizome, which is an underground stem, not a root.
ginger.good_for: gingerol, the compound behind its heat
ginger.store: Fridge, unpeeled, in a bag. It also freezes well.
ginger.spoil: Soft, wrinkled, mouldy, or dark and dry inside.

grape.fact: Grapes don't ripen any further after picking.
grape.spoil: Soft, wrinkled, leaking or mouldy grapes.

grapefruit.fact: A cross between a pomelo and a sweet orange. It can interact with some medicines, so check if you take any.
grapefruit.store: Counter for a week, fridge for longer.
grapefruit.keeps: About 1 week on the counter, 2–3 weeks in the fridge.
grapefruit.spoil: Soft or mouldy spots, wrinkled skin, sour smell.

guava.fact: Some varieties have more vitamin C than an orange.
guava.store: Ripen on the counter; refrigerate once ripe.
guava.keeps: Ripe: about 2–4 days in the fridge.
guava.spoil: Very soft, brown or black patches, mould, fermented smell.

kiwi.fact: Named after New Zealand's fuzzy brown kiwi bird.
kiwi.store: Ripen on the counter, then refrigerate.
kiwi.keeps: Ripe: up to about a week in the fridge.
kiwi.spoil: Very soft or mushy, wrinkled skin, sour smell, mould.

lemon.fact: Lemon juice keeps cut apples and avocados from browning.
lemon.store: Fridge, in a bag: they stay juicy much longer than on the counter.
lemon.keeps: About 1 week on the counter, 2–4 weeks in the fridge.
lemon.spoil: Soft spots, green or white mould, hard shrivelled skin.

lettuce.fact: Mostly water, which is why it wilts so quickly.
lettuce.store: Fridge, dry, wrapped in a paper towel inside a bag.
lettuce.spoil: Slimy or brown leaves, wilting, sour smell.

lime.fact: Most limes in shops are Persian limes, not the smaller key limes.
lime.keeps: About 1 week on the counter, up to 3–4 weeks in the fridge.
lime.spoil: Hard, yellowed, shrivelled skin, soft spots, mould.

lychee.fact: Its bumpy red shell turns brown within days of picking.
lychee.store: Fridge, in a bag, in the shell.
lychee.spoil: Brown, leaking or sour-smelling flesh, mould. A browned shell alone can still be fine inside.

mango.fact: India grows more mangoes than any other country.
mango.store: Ripen on the counter; refrigerate once ripe.
mango.keeps: Ripe: about 5 days in the fridge.
mango.spoil: Very mushy, spreading black spots, oozing, sour or alcoholic smell.

melon.fact: Melons are in the same family as cucumbers and squash.
melon.store: Whole: counter until ripe, then fridge. Scrub the rind before cutting; keep cut melon covered in the fridge.
melon.spoil: Wet soft spots, mould, fermented smell.

mushroom.store: Fridge, in a paper bag rather than plastic.
mushroom.spoil: Slimy, dark spots, wrinkling, sour smell.

nectarine.fact: Essentially a peach without fuzz: a single gene makes the difference.
nectarine.store: Ripen on the counter; refrigerate once ripe.
nectarine.keeps: Ripe: about 3–5 days in the fridge.
nectarine.spoil: Very soft, wrinkled, leaking, mould, brown mushy flesh.

okra.fact: Its slime, called mucilage, is what thickens gumbo.
okra.store: Fridge, dry, in a paper bag.
okra.spoil: Slimy outside, dark spots, soft or mouldy pods.

onion.fact: Cutting one releases a gas that makes your eyes water.
onion.store: Whole: cool, dry, airy place, away from potatoes. Cut: fridge, covered.
onion.keeps: Whole: several weeks; cut: about a week in the fridge.
onion.spoil: Soft or mushy spots, mould, liquid, sprouting.

orange.fact: Brazil grows more oranges than any other country.
orange.store: Counter for about a week, fridge for longer.
orange.keeps: About 1 week on the counter, 2–3 weeks in the fridge.
orange.spoil: Soft or mouldy spots (blue-green or white), sour smell, wrinkled skin.

papaya.fact: Its black seeds are edible and taste peppery.
papaya.store: Ripen on the counter; refrigerate once ripe.
papaya.keeps: Ripe: about 2–3 days in the fridge.
papaya.spoil: Mushy, sunken dark spots, mould, fermented smell.

passion fruit.fact: Wrinkly skin means it's ripe, not rotten.
passion fruit.keeps: Ripe: about a week in the fridge.
passion fruit.spoil: Mould on the skin, very dry and hollow, sour or fermented smell inside.

peach.fact: Peaches belong to the rose family.
peach.store: Ripen stem side down on the counter; refrigerate once ripe.
peach.keeps: Ripe: about 3–5 days in the fridge.
peach.spoil: Very soft, wrinkled, leaking, mould, brown mushy flesh.

pear.fact: Pears ripen from the inside out: if the neck gives a little, it's ready.
pear.store: Ripen on the counter; refrigerate once ripe.
pear.keeps: Ripe: about 3–5 days in the fridge.
pear.spoil: Mushy, brown or leaking flesh, mould, fermented smell.

peas.fact: Peas turn sugar into starch soon after picking, so fresher is sweeter.
peas.spoil: Slimy or mouldy pods, yellowing, sour smell.

pepper.fact: Botanically a fruit, from mild and sweet to fiery hot.
pepper.store: Fridge crisper drawer, whole and unwashed.
pepper.spoil: Soft or wrinkled skin, sunken wet spots, mould.

persimmon.fact: Astringent varieties are only pleasant once they're jelly-soft.
persimmon.keeps: Ripe: a few days in the fridge.
persimmon.spoil: Mould, leaking, fermented smell, spreading black patches.

pineapple.fact: It doesn't get sweeter after picking, though it does soften.
pineapple.store: Whole: counter for a day or two, or fridge. Cut: fridge, covered.
pineapple.spoil: Soft, wet or dark spots, vinegary smell, mould at the base.

plum.fact: The dusty white coating, called bloom, is natural and protects the fruit.
plum.store: Ripen on the counter; refrigerate once ripe.
plum.keeps: Ripe: about 3–5 days in the fridge.

pomegranate.fact: One fruit can hold several hundred juicy seeds, called arils.
pomegranate.store: Whole: counter for a week or fridge for longer. Arils: fridge, covered.
pomegranate.keeps: Whole: several weeks in the fridge; arils: about 5 days.
pomegranate.spoil: Soft, brown or mouldy patches, sour smell, brown mushy arils.

potato.fact: Green patches and sprouts contain solanine, so cut them away before cooking.
potato.store: Cool, dark, dry place, not the fridge, and away from onions.
potato.spoil: Soft, wrinkled, slimy or mouldy, or a strong smell.

pumpkin.fact: Pumpkins are a kind of winter squash.
pumpkin.store: Whole: cool, dry place. Cut: fridge, covered.
pumpkin.keeps: Whole: a month or more; cut: about 5 days.
pumpkin.spoil: Soft or sunken spots, mould, leaking, sour smell.

radish.fact: Radishes can go from seed to harvest in about a month.
radish.store: Remove the leaves and refrigerate in a bag.

raspberry.fact: Raspberries are hollow because their core stays on the plant.
raspberry.store: Fridge, unwashed, in a single layer.

spinach.fact: Its iron is harder to absorb than iron from meat, but it's still very nutritious.
spinach.store: Fridge, dry, in a bag with a paper towel.
spinach.spoil: Slimy, dark or wilted leaves, sour smell.

squash.fact: Summer squash have soft skins; winter squash have hard rinds and keep for months.
squash.store: Winter squash: cool, dry place. Summer squash: fridge.
squash.keeps: Winter: a month or more; summer: up to a week.
squash.spoil: Soft or mushy spots, mould, wrinkling, leaking.

strawberry.fact: The only fruit that wears its seeds on the outside, around 200 per berry.
strawberry.store: Fridge, unwashed, in a single layer. Wash just before eating.
strawberry.spoil: Mushy, leaking, grey or white fuzzy mould. If one is mouldy, throw out any touching it.

sweet potato.fact: Not closely related to regular potatoes: it's in the morning glory family.
sweet potato.store: Cool, dry, dark place, not the fridge.
sweet potato.spoil: Soft, wet or wrinkled spots, mould, dark sunken areas, sour smell.

tamarillo.fact: Also called a tree tomato, it's native to the Andes.
tamarillo.store: Ripen on the counter; refrigerate once ripe.
tamarillo.keeps: Ripe: about a week in the fridge.
tamarillo.spoil: Very soft, wrinkled, mouldy or leaking.

tangerine.fact: A kind of mandarin, and famously easy to peel.
tangerine.store: Counter for a few days, fridge for longer.
tangerine.keeps: About 1 week on the counter, 2 weeks in the fridge.
tangerine.spoil: Soft or mouldy spots, sour smell, dry segments.

tomato.fact: Botanically a fruit, but cooked and eaten like a vegetable.
tomato.store: Counter, stem side down, until ripe. Refrigerate only once very ripe, then let it warm up before eating.
tomato.keeps: Ripe: a few days on the counter.
tomato.spoil: Soft or sunken spots, splits, leaking, mould, black patches, sour smell.

turnip.fact: Young turnips are sweet enough to eat raw.
turnip.store: Remove the greens and refrigerate in a bag.
turnip.spoil: Soft, spongy, shrivelled, slimy or mouldy.

watermelon.fact: About 92% water, which is where the name comes from.
watermelon.store: Whole: counter or fridge. Scrub the rind before cutting; keep cut pieces covered in the fridge.
watermelon.keeps: Whole: about 1–2 weeks; cut: about 3–5 days.
watermelon.spoil: Mushy or slimy flesh, sour or fizzy smell, mould.

zucchini.fact: A summer squash, usually picked young.
zucchini.spoil: Soft, wrinkled, slimy or mouldy, especially at the ends.
